title: ～割に — “considering ～ / for ～”
summary: Compares a result with what you would normally expect from a standard: “considering A, B is (surprisingly) …”. It attaches to a plain-form verb or adjective (な-adj + な), or noun + の. The result can be better or worse than expected.

patterns.gloss: for ～ (e.g. 手間がかかる割に)
for the price / age (値段の割に, 年の割に)

body.p: A is the standard (price, effort, age); B is the real result that does not match it. 値段の割においしい: good for the price. Whether it is positive or negative depends on B.
Verbs and い-adjectives use the plain form (手間がかかる割に). な-adjectives take な (有名な割に). Nouns take の (年の割に). Adding は (割には) makes the contrast a little stronger.
～のに also shows an unexpected result, but ～割に always has a standard that you compare to (price, age, effort). ～にしては is close and refers to a specific situation. ～割に is not used with a person’s will.

examples.ja: この店（みせ）は値段（ねだん）の割（わり）においしい。
examples.romaji: Kono mise wa nedan no wari ni oishii.
examples.tr: This shop is tasty considering the price.

examples.ja: この料理（りょうり）は手間（てま）がかかる割（わり）に、味（あじ）は普通（ふつう）だ。
examples.romaji: Kono ryouri wa tema ga kakaru wari ni, aji wa futsuu da.
examples.tr: This dish takes a lot of effort, but for that the taste is only ordinary.

examples.ja: 年（とし）を取（と）っている割（わり）に、あの人（ひと）はとても元気（げんき）だ。
examples.romaji: Toshi o totte iru wari ni, ano hito wa totemo genki da.
examples.tr: For their age, that person is remarkably energetic.

pitfalls: The main clause must be an evaluation or fact, not an order or the speaker’s will (×割に頑張ろう).
Remember の after a noun (値段の割に), not に directly.
